newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CNB plan sees foreigners in bank selloff.
newsitem.headline: Czech CNB plan sees foreigners in bank selloff.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) has submitted a proposal to cabinet which calls for foreign investors to participate in the privatisation of the country's four largest banks, the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny reported on Tuesday.

The paper quoted central bank vice-governor Pavel Kysilka as saying that partners for the "Big Four" banks, which are still controlled by the state, should bring know-how and banking ethics, as well as increased financial strength.
The "Big Four" comprise Komercni Banka a.s., Ceska Sporitelna a.s., Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. (CSOB), and IPB a.s..
Government officials have expressed willingness to continue the sell-off of state holdings in banks, with the exception of CSOB, which began earlier in the post-communist transformation process.

Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said recently that IPB, where the state holds around 30 percent, would be the first to go completely private. London-based Nomura Internaitonal and Dutch bank ING NV have been reported as leading parties interested in IPB.
The paper said Kysilka was not opposed to the idea of foreign portfolio investors taking stakes in the banks.
But he said he would not support "privatisation at any cost" which would bring strong but untransparent investors, including some of the domestic groups, the paper added.

It quoted the vice-governor as saying that if the state kept small stakes of about five percent in the privatised banks, it would tell management that the state had no rights, only obligations, in the banks.
